recipes.name: Eggplant Pizzas
ingredients_raw: 1 large eggplant, sliced into 1/2 inch rounds

steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Beat the eggs in a bowl. Mix the flour, salt, pepper, and oregano in a 1 gallon resealable plastic bag. Dip each eggplant slice in the egg, then drop the eggplant in the flour mixture one at a time, shaking the bag to coat the eggplant.

Heat the vegetable oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat. Place the eggplant slices in the skillet to cook, turning occasionally, until evenly browned. Drain the eggplant slices on a paper towel-lined plate. Arrange the eggplant in one layer on a baking sheet. Spoon enough pizza sauce to cover each eggplant slice. Top each eggplant with mozzarella cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until the mozzarella cheese is melted, 5 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Eggplant Pizzas
raw_recipe.description: A lightly fried slice of eggplant replaces the dough in this versatile pizza.

review.reviewBody: I'm giving this 5 stars because my entire family liked it (kids are almost two and four and a half). Score! I didn't fry it first mostly because I needed my hands to do other things to get dinner ready in a hurry. I followed the direction exactly except after I floured them I also dipped them in panko. I put them on a greased cookie sheet and baked on 450 for about 20 mins. Once they can be pierced with a fork, I took them out and put tomato sauce, a generous amount of parmesan and then grated mozzarella and put them back in at 350 for about 5-10 minutes to melt cheese. Baking them made them plenty crispy and really delicious! My guess is too much oil could make them soggy if you weren't careful.

This recipe was great and fun! Here's what I did differently. 1). I coated the eggplant in eggs and breadcrumbs rather than flour and since they were seasoned it gave the pizzas a bit of flavor. When I fried them I used just enough oil to coat the pan and they dried them w/ a paper towel before baking 2). I added veggie italian sausage, mushrooms and onion and I stir-fried the veggies a bit first so they were tender.

This recipe was even liked by my very picky 5-year old daughter (of course I just told her they were pizzas, but after she ate 2 I told her it was eggplant and she didn't believe me!).

Really quite good. I took the recommendation of others and floured, egged then dipped these slices in italian breadcrumbs. After greasing a cookie sheet with olive oil, I cooked these for 20 mins at 450. Then topped with sauce, parm and mozz cheeses and a mix of mushrooms, onions, garlic, and red peppers. bake again for 8 minutes on 350. Like homemade tapas! Please make. So easy and came out crispy and perfect.

These are very fun to eat and were easy to make! I tweaked the recipe and I’m glad I did. Like others, I flowered, egged and coated the slices with Italian breadcrumbs. They were crispy and flavorful. I didn’t put them in the skillet, instead straight in the oven. I also added fun toppings like mushrooms and tomatoes. Fun meal.

Like everyone else, I baked the eggplant instead of frying. I added more of the seasonings to the flour, and also added garlic and parsley. Two medium eggplant filled up an entire half-sheet pan. Hubby loved it! Next time I’ll try to get the eggplant crispy by cutting the eggplant thinner (1/4”), adding Parmesan cheese to the breading, and flipping half way through baking.

Followed different directions and it turned out fantastic. The kids ate seconds despite bemoaning eggplant being the main ingredient. Similar to what's recommended below, I dredged the sliced eggplant in beaten egg then Italian breadcrumbs and baked on a lightly olive 'oiled' cookie sheet at 400F for 20 minutes. I removed and while hot spooned on the pizza sauce and shredded mozzarella cheese with a dash of oregano on top. They went back in the oven for 8 minutes at 350 degrees. After coming out I let them rest but a minute before the ravenous bunch took over. They were delish, loved by all and beyond easy.

I dipped in egg white, then in a mixture of breadcrumbs and flour mix. Then baked at 450º for 20 minutes in stead of frying. While it was baking I carmelized some yellow onions and then added mushroom, a little sherry and garlic. Topped the eggplant with tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, and onion/mushroom mixture and even my "eggplant hating husband" was raving about these. My son said he could be a vegetarian if the food was this good! These could be good appetizers if the eggplant was thin and made smaller rounds.

I also baked these instead of frying (450 degrees for 20 minutes). And I topped them with a variety of toppings - diced ham, spinach, mushrooms & red onions - all chopped into small pieces and sauteed prior to topping. Finally, I used pepper jack cheese as I did not have mozzarella. Even my husband loved these and he is not usually very fond of dishes that substitute pasta/bread with veggies.

Made a version of these and they were really good but honestly there is NO NEED TO FRY ???? Just dip the eggplant in egg and breading of your choice and bake turning once it you like on sheet with parchment and 
spray oil. Then spread your marinara add your sauteed veges and cheese of choice and bake until melted!!! So good!!!

Delicious! Like Filaree, I skipped the frying. I just dipped them in egg, sprinkled salt and garlic seasoning, baked them for 20 minutes at 450, topped them with tomato sauce, parmesean, and mozzarella, and then baked them for another 6 minutes. Plenty crispy. I feel like frying them would have been gross! Next time I might try to dip them in almond flour instead of wheat flour (I try to avoid wheat whenever possible).

Very good. Seasoned bread crumbs are a must along with italian seasoning and red pepper flakes. I served them on pasta with the remaining marinara. The last batch was forgotten and left in the oven for a good 35 minutes. They baked into crisp little nuggets which were incredibly delicious!

On the suggestion of the submitter, I topped with pepperoni and mushroom. Instead of baking, I would air fry at 375F for 6-8 minutes, crisps the pizzas better. If I were to bake again, I would turn the oven way up to like 425-450F.
Delicious! Essentially like eggplant parmesan, just with pizza toppings. Used the oven to crisp it up as opposed to the frying. Thanks for the recipe!
The eggplant was mushy. I was hoping for crisp crust, but I should have listened to the commenters and tried breadcrumbs.
It was delicious, I didn't change anything!
this is a great twist to pizza and very tasty. I baked it and seasoned with fresh herb. it was very good and full of flavor,

8-7-22 Excellent idea. I did coat each slice with homemade Italian bread crumbs after dipping in the egg because I like crunch. I baked the slices (25 minutes at 350, turn 25 minutes at 375) as I also needed to make pizza sauce and side dishes. Cutting into 1/2 inch slices made the pizzas not only sturdy but also soft.
So good! I added other “pizza” toppings this was amazing! Thank you

These were quick and easy to make, and they’re delicious! If you made too many, save the breaded cooked eggplant without sauce and cheese. The next day, put the sauce and cheese on, and reheat. They are great!
My husband is technically the chef in our home, but this recipe made me a hero in our kitchen! So good, so easy, and everyone in our family of 7 loved it! Thank you!!
